subject: POC Trial Environment: hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC (next steps)
snippet: Recap from today's call: define success criteria, choose environment (hosted vs dedicated sandbox vs VPC), assign owners, and confirm timeline for 2-week POC.
messages:

Subject: Quick follow-up from today's discovery

Thanks again for the demo this morning — that was super helpful. A couple of clarifying points from our side as we think about the POC:

- Primary success criteria: reduce latency for our chat assistant to under 250ms p50 and validate semantic similarity quality vs our current embedding pipeline.
- Data constraints: we cannot send customer PII to third-party hosted environments during the trial; we can use synthetic or anonymized records.
- Timeline: we'd like a 2-3 week hands-on trial starting early March if we can get an environment provisioned.

Can you confirm which environment option makes the most sense given our constraints: hosted Redwood trial (with anonymized data), dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool), or a VPC/private deployment for the trial? Also please send a short checklist of items your team needs from us to kick off.

Thanks,

Thanks Alex — great notes. Recap + next steps below.

Recap (call takeaways):
- Success criteria (as discussed): p50 latency < 250ms on representative chat requests; embedding recall > current baseline on our evaluation set; no PII sent to hosted environments.
- Evaluation plan: 1) run representative request set against Redwood hosted trial (anonymized data) OR dedicated sandbox; 2) measure latency/cost and embedding quality; 3) validate integration points (prefix caching, KV cache behavior) and failure/fallback behavior.
- Timeline: target 2-week POC beginning week of Mar 8; prep work in the week prior.
- Owners: Marissa (Redwood) — POC coordinator; Rishi — commercial/contract lead; Dev — technical SRE/engineer for environment setup; Alex/Jordan (Acme) — data and infra owners.

Environment options (pros/cons):
1) Hosted trial (fastest): Redwood-hosted model endpoints, anonymized data only. Pros: quickest to spin up, minimal infra work. Cons: cannot accept PII, limited network integration.
2) Dedicated sandbox (reserved GPU pool): Redwood-managed GPUs dedicated to Acme for trial period. Pros: predictable performance, supports larger seq lengths and custom kernel tuning. Cons: >2 business days to provision; still not full VPC networking.
3) VPC trial (private): Private deployment in your VPC or our Private offering; supports full network controls and PII policies. Pros: meets PII requirement, full audit controls. Cons: provisioning and security review required (usually 1-2 weeks).

Kickoff checklist (what we need from Acme to start):
- Confirm which environment option you prefer.
- Provide anonymized sample dataset and eval set (or sign an NDA for limited PII access if VPC).
- Point of contact for infra (VPC subnet/cidr if VPC) and a contact to approve firewall rules.
- If Dedicated/Sandbox: expected throughput (requests/sec) and peak prompt lengths.

Next steps: If you confirm hosted, we can schedule setup this week and start the POC by Mar 8. If you choose VPC, we'll open a security questionnaire and schedule a short network design call.

I'll attach a draft SOW and a simple network diagram for the VPC option.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
